source.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: Expand a Euclidean bilinear form in coordinates. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source.original_text:
Let H be a continuous real bilinear form on a finite-dimensional Euclidean coordinate space. Evaluating H on vectors x and y gives the sum over ordered coordinate pairs of their coordinates multiplied by the corresponding basis entry.

The coordinate type is finite with decidable equality. The vectors eᵢ are the standard Euclidean orthonormal basis.
H is linear in each argument and continuous. The vectors x and y are arbitrary.

H(x,y)=\sum_i\sum_j x_i y_j\,H(e_i,e_j).

lean.statement:
theorem anonymous_target.{u_1}
  {I : Type u_1} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] (H : EuclideanSpace ℝ I →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ I →L[ℝ] ℝ)
  (x y : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) :
  (H x) y = ∑ i, ∑ j, x.ofLp i * y.ofLp j * (H ((EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ) i)) ((EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ) j)

blind_reconstruction.text:
Objects: H is a continuous real bilinear form written as a continuous linear map E -> (E -> R); e_i is the standard coordinate basis vector.

Domains: I is finite with decidable equality; E=EuclideanSpace(R,I); H:E->L[R](E->L[R]R); x,y in E.

Quantifiers: Universally I,its instances,H,x,y.

Assumptions: No symmetry, positivity, or normalization of H,x,y is assumed beyond H's bundled continuity and linearity.

Conclusion: H(x)(y)=sum_{i in I} sum_{j in I} x_i*y_j*H(e_i)(e_j).

Scopes: An exact finite double-sum identity over the whole index type; no convergence or probabilistic scope. H need not be symmetric.

Constant dependencies: The coefficients are the fixed entries H(e_i)(e_j); no existential constant is asserted.

import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Basis.Bilinear

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.EuclideanBilinearCoordinates

open scoped BigOperators

/-- The ordered coordinate expansion of a continuous bilinear form on Euclidean space. -/
theorem euclidean_bilinear_eq_sum_basis
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (H : EuclideanSpace ℝ I →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ I →L[ℝ] ℝ)
    (x y : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) :
    H x y = ∑ i : I, ∑ j : I,
      x i * y j * H (EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ i) (EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ j) := by
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ I
  let e := EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ
  let L : E →ₗ[ℝ] E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ :=
    (ContinuousLinearMap.coeLM ℝ : (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ).comp H.toLinearMap
  have h := LinearMap.sum_repr_mul_repr_mul e.toBasis e.toBasis (B := L) x y
  simpa [Finsupp.sum_fintype, L, e, EuclideanSpace.basisFun_repr, smul_eq_mul, mul_assoc]
    using h.symm

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.EuclideanBilinearCoordinates

steps.title: Use the underlying bilinear map
steps.text: Forget continuity in each of the two linear maps. This keeps every evaluation equal.
steps.lean:
let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ I
  let e := EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ
  let L : E →ₗ[ℝ] E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ :=
    (ContinuousLinearMap.coeLM ℝ : (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ).comp H.toLinearMap

steps.title: Apply the basis expansion
steps.text: The algebraic bilinear basis theorem expands both arguments. In the standard Euclidean basis the representation coefficients are the actual coordinates.
steps.lean:
have h := LinearMap.sum_repr_mul_repr_mul e.toBasis e.toBasis (B := L) x y
  simpa [Finsupp.sum_fintype, L, e, EuclideanSpace.basisFun_repr, smul_eq_mul, mul_assoc]
    using h.symm
